#Finance Department 
```{r}
#checking if we are allowed to scrape this info

robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/fsb/directory/?up=/query/all/all/Accountancy/all",
  domain = "https://miamioh.edu"
)

# I will load the backend of the HTML into R using 
# rvest::read_html() | sometimes rvest::read_html_live() if the page has some dynamic content
# in come cases we will craft this as a request as shown in the slides httr2:: request()>....> httr2::resp_body_html()


finance_courses_in_r = rvest::read_html("https://miamioh.edu/fsb/directory/?up=/query/all/all/Accountancy/all")

# I will extract the course departments 

# CSSS selector was obtained by:
# Highlighting what we wanted to pull (Department) -> then I right clicked inspect then I clicked copy selector
finance_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1)")|>
  rvest::html_text2()->finance_titles

# course descriptions [using selector gadget does not always work]
# but when it works it is easier

finance_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a")|>
  rvest::html_text2()->finance_names



finance_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3)")|>
  rvest::html_text2()->finance_roles




```


multiple websites 


```{r}
# enable you to scrape multiple webpages (from the same site) using a 'for loop type

# Enable you to scrape multiple webpages (from the same site) using the [purrr package](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/), which is a functional programming approach (in this process we will create our own function)


dept_abbrv = c("Accountancy", "Economics", "Entrepreneurship", "Finance", "Information Systems & Analytics", "Marketing", "Management")

courses_df = data.frame()

for (abbrv in dept_abbrv) {
  cat( rep("-", 50), "\n")
  
  print(abbrv)
  
  dept_url = paste0('https://miamioh.edu/fsb/directory/?up=/query/all/all/', URLencode(abbrv), '/all')


webpage = rvest::read_html(dept_url)

#DEPARTMENT

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1)") |> rvest::html_text2()->department


#NAME

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_text2()->name


webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3)") |> rvest::html_text2()->roles


df = data.frame(department = department, name = name, position = roles)

courses_df = rbind(courses_df,df)

}

head()

```



```{r}

dept_abbrv = c("Accountancy", "Economics", "Entrepreneurship", "Finance", "Information Systems & Analytics", "Marketing", "Management")
scrape_proffessors = function(abbrv){
  
  dept_url = paste0('https://miamioh.edu/fsb/directory/?up=/query/all/all/', URLencode(abbrv), '/all')


webpage = rvest::read_html(dept_url)

#DEPARTMENT

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(1)") |> rvest::html_text2()->department


#NAME

webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_text2()->name


webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3)") |> rvest::html_text2()->roles

#WEBSITE
webpage |> rvest::html_elements("tr > td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_attr("href")->website

df = data.frame(department = department, name = name, position = roles, website = website)


return(df)
}

test = scrape_proffessors(abbrv = "Finance")

# to use functions from purr, we will use a map_*() or a map2_*(), or a pmap_*()
# map uses a function that takes a single input (or you are only chaning a single input)
# map2 uses a function that takes two inputs
# pmap>=3
# after the _, you put the type of object you are getting back

courses_df_from = purrr::map_df(.x = dept_abbrv, .f = scrape_proffessors)

head(courses_df_from)

```
